(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.G.S.KAMAL) Petitioners herein are before this Court seeking following reliefs :
a) Issue a writ in the nature of certiorari quash the impugned online notification dated 27-11-2023 bearing No.Dg../PAUg/ -/2023-24 in Form No.2-e vide Annexure-G passed by the 2nd respondent and consequently quash the M.R.No.T168 dated 15.12.2023 passed by respondent No.4 vide Annexure-H.
b) issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing respondent No.4 to restore the name of petitioners to the extent of 06 acres 27 guntas in Sy.No.112/3 situated at Hegdiyal village, Taluk and Dist.
Vijayapur.
c) Issue such other writ or order or direction as this Hon'ble court deems just and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case and allow this writ petition.
2. Case of the petitioners is that the land bearing Sy.No.112/3 measuring 06 acres 27 guntas situated at Hegdiyal L.T. Village, Vijayapura District and Taluk is owned and possessed by the ancestors of the petitioners namely Limbu Gemu Lamani, he having purchased the same in terms of registered deed of sale dated NC: 2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR 26.10.1938.
His name was mutated in the revenue records on 26.10.1938.

The said Limbu Gemu Lamani and his brother by name Meetu Gemu Lamani effected partition, in which, land in Sy.No.112/3, measuring 06 acres 27 guntas has been allotted to the share of Limbu Gemu Lamani.
3. In furtherance therefore, name of Limbu Gemu Lamani came to be mutated vide Mutation No.1276 on 30.09.1965.

Said Limbu Gemu Lamani passed away leaving behind his sons and daughters namely Shivu, Yanku, Basu, Puradu, Karevva, Sitabai and Kamalabai, whose names were mutated in the revenue records vide Mutation No.1321 dated 21.07.1965.
Petitioners are the legal heirs and their names came to be mutated in the revenue records to the extent of 06 acre 27 guntas vide Mutation No.2983 on 30.09.1993.
Thus, the petitioners have been in actual possession and enjoyment of the aforesaid property and there is no other agricultural land standing in the name of the petitioners.

Since they belonged to the Lamani community, they are used to NC:
2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR residing near the agricultural lands along with their community members.

4. Things stood thus, respondent No.2 without holding any enquiry issued notification under Section 38A of the Land Reforms Act (Amendment) 2016 with effect from 28.10.2017, declaring the Kesu vs The State Of Karnataka on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123930754/

sentences.text: Basavanagar as an unrecorded habitation based on the proposal purportedly sent by respondent No.2 -Assistant Commissioner.

The said recommendation was issued without issuing any notice and providing any opportunity, the extent of land which is sought to be included under the unrecorded habitation area is about 03 acres 32 guntas out of 06 acres 27 guntas of land in Sy.No.112/3 belonging to the petitioners.

That subsequent issuance of notification, name of the Government and Basavanagar came to be mutated vide M.R.No.T168 dated 15.12.2023.
5.
All these proceedings have been held behind the back of the petitioners.
Respondents on 14.10.2025 came near the land of the petitioners on the pretext of NC: 2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR measuring the same.
It is only then the petitioners learnt about the respondent-authorities having issued the notification on 27.11.2023.
Being aggrieved with the present petition.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioners relies upon the order dated 28.02.2025 passed in W.P.No.103107/2022 as well as order dated 11.11.2025 passed in W.P.No.201276/2025 submits that under identical facts of the matter this Court has quashed the notification and directed the respondents to consider the representation of the petitioners therein and to pass appropriate orders after holding an enquiry as contemplated under law.
He submits that the petitioners herein who are similarly situated may also be extended with similar benefits.

7. Learned Additional Government Advocate however submits that even before issuance of notification, a survey would have been conducted and without conducting such a survey, the inhabited area would not be NC: 2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR carved out.

He however submits that the petitioners since claiming that they have not issued any notice or opportunity, a direction will be issued to the petitioners to submit a representation which will be considered in accordance with law.

8. Submission taken on record.
9.

Provisions of Section 38A of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 read with Rule 9B to 9E of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1974 elaborately set-out the procedure for issuing grant certificate of ownership to the agricultural labourers.

10. Perusal of the notification at Annexure-G indicates that the declaration of lands including the land of the petitioners is shown as unrecorded habitation falling within Basava Nagar, merely, on the basis of a report submitted by the Assistant Commissioner of Raichur, Sub- Division.
Annexure-G further indicates that no notice of proceedings have been initiated, before issuing the same.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR 11.
The records submitted by the petitioners produce at Annexures-A to F indicate that the name of the petitioners has continued in the revenue records.

12. The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court under the similar circumstances, in its order dated 28.02.2025 passed in W.P.No.103107/2022 in the case of Shamanna and others vs. State of Kesu vs The State Of Karnataka on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123930754/
4 Karnataka and others, had quashed similar notification directing the Deputy Commissioner to verify the revenue records and thereafter to pass appropriate order, with liberty, in the event of Deputy Commissioner coming to the conclusion that the lands required for public purpose, to initiate acquisition proceedings in accordance with applicable law.

sentences.text:
Similarly, this Court taking note of the aforesaid order of the Coordinate Bench by order dated 11.11.2025 passed in W.P.No.201276/2025 had quashed the impugned notification, directing the respondents to consider the representation of petitioner and after enquiry, if it was found the petitioner is indeed the owner and NC:
2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR possessor of the land to restore his name in the revenue records.

13. In that view of the matter, the petition is allowed in the following directions :
i) Notification dated 27.11.2023 produced at Annexure-G issued by respondent No.2 - Deputy Commissioner, to the extent of the land measuring 03 acres 32 guntas in Sy.No.112/3 belonging to the petitioners is quashed.
ii) Petitioners shall submit a representation along with document justifying their entitlements within 15 days from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
iii) Upon submission of such representation, respondent No.2 - Deputy Commissioner shall consider the representation.
After holding an enquiry as contemplated under law, pass orders one way or the other, communicate the same to the petitioners in writing within 90 days thereafter.

iv) Respondent No.2 -Deputy Commissioner shall undertake the exercise as directed above and - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7353 HC-KAR pass appropriate orders within 3 months on the date of petitioners submitting the representation as directed.
v) After the enquiry, if it is found that the petitioners are indeed the owners in possession of the land in Sy.No.112/3 measuring 06 acres 27 guntas as claimed, and if the said land is required by respondent-authorities, necessary proceedings be initiated and the compensation, if any, be paid to the petitioners in accordance with law.
 vi) Since the document produced at  Annexure-H to the writ petition dated 27.11.2023 indicate the name of the petitioners being reflected in the revenue records vide M.R.No.T168 and in the light of the notification having been passed as above, names of the petitioners will be restored, till the order as directed above is passed.
